title: Hospital referrals to housing first: outcomes of referred patients and barriers to referral, a convergent mixed methods study
abstract: Objective: to describe housing outcomes and hospital use of inpatients referred to housing first and to explain what helps or blocks referral. Design: convergent mixed methods study with a quantitative strand on 2024 and 2025 referrals and a matched comparison of emergency use, and peer-led interviews with referred people and staff. Results and conclusions will be written after both strands are complete.
introduction: Hospital referral to housing first is a promising route out of homelessness, but hospital referrals are accepted less often than outreach referrals, and outcomes after hospital referral are rarely followed.
methods: Referred inpatients were followed for tenancy start and emergency use; eligible non-referred inpatients were matched on prior emergency use and weighted by propensity scores, with a negative control outcome. Interviews were co-led by a peer researcher. Strands were analysed separately and integrated in a joint display.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present housing within six months, predictors of housing, emergency use against the comparison group, themes, and the joint display.
discussion: The discussion will translate integrated findings into the referral pathway and state the limits of the comparison.
limitations: Confounding by engagement; one hospital; interview sample bias.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will not claim that referral causes lower emergency use.
summary: GRAMMS-structured draft with both strands; results empty.
